diagnostic_evidence.quote: As $\calK \in L(\bH, \bH)$ and $\calK \in L(C_b, C_b)$, \Cref{ass:rkhs_invariance} is fulfilled.

Let $k: \bR^n \times \bR^n \to \bR$ be a continuous strictly positive-definite symmetric kernel and $\bH$ the induced reproducing kernel Hilbert space on $\Omega$ with $\calK \in L(\bH,\bH)$ and ${\calK \in L(C_b(\Omega),C_b(\Omega))}$.

issues.failure_explanation: The hypotheses constrain only the Koopman operator, not the kernel k. For an admissible instance with a positive-definite but not strictly positive-definite kernel (e.g. k≡1, whose RKHS is the constant functions, with K the identity), K_X is singular for d≥2, so K_X^{-1} in (eq:total_err) and in the approximant (eq:mcedmd) is undefined; and ‖k‖_∞ can be infinite, while the proof's Hoeffding step needs |(S_X f)(y)| ≤ ‖k‖_∞^{1/2}‖f‖_H. The proof's assertion that its hypotheses imply the standing assumption ass:rkhs_invariance (which contains continuity, symmetry and strict positive definiteness of k) is a false inference: K ∈ L(H,H) and K ∈ L(C_b,C_b) concern the transition kernel, not k.

failure_location.quote: Let $\bH$ be an RKHS of functions over $\Omega$, and assume $\calK\in L(\mathbb{H}, \mathbb{H})$ and $\calK\in L(C_b(\Omega),C_b(\Omega))$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add to thm:total_error_bound the kernel hypotheses of ass:rkhs_invariance (k continuous, symmetric, strictly positive definite; pairwise distinct design points), i.e. the setting in which the proof actually operates.
issues.overall_effect: The main theorem is ill-defined (or vacuous when ‖k‖_∞=∞) for RKHSs admitted by its stated hypotheses; cor:reg_total_err_bound, whose hypotheses are 'the assumptions of thm:total_error_bound' with no kernel specified, inherits the defect (e.g. λ=0 with singular K_X). The Section 4 development under ass:rkhs_invariance is unaffected.
issues.title: Headline L∞-error bound stated without the kernel hypotheses needed for well-definedness
issues.why_classification: Local addition of standard hypotheses already used throughout Section 4; all bounds, rates and the high-probability guarantee survive unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Assume that $\calK \in L(C_b, C_b)$ and that \eqref{e:hl_charac} is satisfied for some $\ell \in \bN$ with $\ell > \sigma_{n, l}$.
Assume that $\calK \in L(\bH, \bH)$ and $\calK \in L(C_b(\Omega), C_b(\Omega))$.

issues.failure_explanation: cor:det_err_wendland requires the invariance-characterization condition (e:hl_charac) at some integer level ℓ > σ_{n,l}. thm:total_err_wendland assumes only K ∈ L(H,H) and K ∈ L(C_b,C_b), which does not imply (e:hl_charac) at any level (that would require H^ℓ-invariance for ℓ > σ_{n,l}, strictly stronger than boundedness on H^{σ_{n,l}}). The deterministic term of the bound is thus taken from a result used outside its hypotheses. The claim itself is true and follows from thm:err1 plus the fill-distance projection bound [Wend04, Thm 11.17], both applicable under the theorem's hypotheses.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the citation of cor:det_err_wendland by thm:err1 combined with the Wendland projection-error bound ‖I−S_X‖_{H→C_b} ≤ C h_X^{l+1} from [Wend04, Thm 11.17].
issues.overall_effect: As written, the proof of the deterministic term of thm:total_err_wendland is unsupported; the statement, rate and probability guarantee are independently recoverable.
issues.title: Wendland error bound proved via a corollary invoked outside its hypotheses
issues.why_classification: One-step citation swap with in-source ingredients; no statement, rate or guarantee changes.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: By part (ii) of \Cref{thm:hs_frac_charac}, this implies that $H^s$ is invariant under $\calK$ for all $s \in (0, \ell]$.

issues.failure_explanation: Since ‖z‖_{H^{-|α|}} ≥ ‖z‖_{H^{-ℓ}} for |α| ≤ ℓ, the stated condition is strictly stronger than what the proofs establish. In the 'invariance ⇒ condition' direction (Steps 1–2) the chain bounds |⟨Kf,D^αφ⟩| by C‖f‖_{H^ℓ}‖φ‖ with f ranging over H^ℓ, yielding H^{-ℓ}-norms; for |α| < ℓ the H^{-|α|}-norm requires a supremum over f ∈ H^{|α|} with ‖f‖_{H^{|α|}}=1, for which the argument gives nothing (‖f‖_{H^ℓ} is not controlled by ‖f‖_{H^{|α|}}), and no interpolation argument is supplied. Already at ℓ=1 the |α|=0 term is concluded (as written) only as an H^{-1}-bound where H^{0}=L² is required. Conversely, Step 5 derives only ∑‖dν_{D^αφ}/dx‖_{H^{-ℓ}} ≤ C‖φ‖ and then invokes part (ii), which as stated requires the stronger H^{-|α|} condition — an inference that fails as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace H^{-|α|} by H^{-ℓ} in (e:hl_charac): every proof step (Steps 1, 2 and 5) then verifies the restated condition, and the iff-characterization, parts (ii)–(iii) and all downstream invariance results go through. (Alternatively, complete the stronger H^{-|α|}-version via the paper's interpolation machinery and H^{-|α|}-bounds in Step 5.)
issues.overall_effect: Part (i)'s 'only if' direction is unproven as stated, and the proof of part (iii) — hence of thm:diff_density_hs_invariance and the invariance conclusion of prop:trunc_norm — contains an invalid inference.
issues.title: Invariance characterization (e:hl_charac) stated with H^{-|α|} norms but only established and applied at the H^{-ℓ} level
issues.why_classification: A one-index restatement yields an equivalent characterization (both versions are equivalent to invariance) and makes all proofs valid; no substantive claim, regime or downstream result is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $\bH\subset C_b(\Omega)$ be a RKHS that is invariant under $\calK$. Then $\calK : \bH\to\bH$ is bounded.
Then $\calK : H^1\to H^1$ is bounded by \Cref{prop:RKHS_inv}.

issues.failure_explanation: prop:RKHS_inv requires an RKHS contained in C_b(Ω); by Sobolev embedding, H^s(Ω) satisfies this only for s > n/2 (a fact the paper itself states). The proof of thm:hs_frac_charac invokes it for H¹ and H^ℓ for arbitrary n and ℓ, in particular when ℓ ≤ n/2, where H^ℓ is not an RKHS of continuous functions. The boundedness of K: H^ℓ → H^ℓ used to derive (e:hl_charac) in the sufficiency direction — and, implicitly, the H^ℓ-boundedness input to the Step-3 interpolation and the K ∈ L(H^s,H^s) conclusion of thm:diff_density_hs_invariance for s ≤ n/2 — is thus unestablished as written.

failure_location.quote: Again, this gives the boundedness of $\calK: H^\ell \to H^\ell$ by \Cref{prop:RKHS_inv}

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the two invocations of prop:RKHS_inv in Steps 1–2 by a closed-graph argument: under (L1), K is bounded on L², so K: H^ℓ → H^ℓ is a closed operator on the Banach space H^ℓ, hence bounded; this requires no RKHS structure.
issues.overall_effect: All boundedness assertions for the Koopman operator on Sobolev spaces with index s ≤ n/2 (the operator-norm constant in the 'only if' direction of (i), the interpolation input in Step 3, and the L(H^s,H^s) claim of thm:diff_density_hs_invariance in that regime) are unsupported as written.
issues.title: Boundedness from H^ℓ-invariance deduced via prop:RKHS_inv outside its RKHS hypothesis
issues.why_classification: Standard three-line functional-analysis substitution; all statements (which are true) survive verbatim.

issues.failure_explanation: With ∂₁G = G·(y−x), the quotient rule gives ∂₁p = (G/H)·((y−x) − H'(x)/H(x)); the displayed formula omits the factor 1/H on the (y−x)-term. The subsequently stated bound corresponds to neither the correct formula (which yields (1/√(2π))(1/C₁ + 1/(√(2π)C₁²))) nor the displayed one (which would give (1/√(2π))(1 + 1/(√(2π)C₁²))). Both the displayed derivative and the stated constant are false as written. The conclusion survives: p is smooth with H bounded above and bounded below away from 0 on (0,1), so ∂₁p is bounded and (e:Hs_condition_density) holds for ℓ=1 with some finite constant. (The proof also never verifies the standing hypothesis (L1) of thm:hs_frac_charac(iii), though it holds here since ‖p‖_{L²(Ω×Ω)} ≤ C implies ∫ρ_x(Δ)dx ≤ |Ω|^{1/2}C|Δ|.)

failure_location.quote: \partial_1 p(x,y) = \frac{\partial_1 G(x,y) H(x) - G(x,y) H'(x)}{H(x)^2} = G(x,y) \left( (y-x) - \frac{H'(x)}{H(x)^2}\right)

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the quotient-rule computation and the resulting constant (any finite bound on ‖∂₁p‖_{L∞((0,1)²)} suffices for (e:Hs_condition_density)); optionally verify (L1).
issues.overall_effect: Only the intermediate displayed formulas and the constant in the proof of prop:trunc_norm are unreliable; the H¹-invariance conclusion itself remains valid after recomputation.
issues.title: Incorrect quotient-rule computation in the truncated-normal invariance example
issues.why_classification: Local recomputation; the proposition's statement, its role as an example, and all downstream uses are unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: we choose a smoothness $l \in \bN$ and set $\beta_{n, l} = \calI^l \beta_{\lfloor \frac{n}{2}\rfloor + l + 1}$

issues.failure_explanation: By the paper's own definition (Appendix B, with (Iβ)(r) = ∫_r^∞ tβ(t)dt), B_{n,l}(0) = (I^l β_{⌊n/2⌋+l+1})(0). For n=1, l=1 this equals ∫₀¹ t(1−t)² dt = 1/12, whereas the claimed formula gives 2^{-1}·binom(3,1) = 3/2. The kernel used in the numerics, normalized to value 1 at r=0, matches neither. The closed form is false for every l ≥ 1 under the paper's definitions (it holds only trivially at l=0).

failure_location.quote: for the Wendland kernel $k_{n, l}$ with RBF $B_{n,l}$, we have $B_{n,l}(0) = \frac{1}{2^l} \binom{\lfloor n/2\rfloor + 2l + 1}{l}$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the false closed form by the correct value (I^l β_{⌊n/2⌋+l+1})(0), or leave B_{n,l}(0) unevaluated/consistent with the chosen normalization.
issues.overall_effect: Only the illustrative constant in rem:kernel_matrix_cond is false; the structural bound ‖K_X^{-1}k_X(x)‖₁² ≤ k(x,x)·d/λ_min(K_X) and all error bounds (which use ‖k‖_∞^{1/2} or C₂ = √(p_{n,l}(0) without this formula) are unaffected.
issues.title: False closed-form value B_{n,l}(0) for the Wendland kernel
issues.why_classification: Isolated false constant in a remark; nothing downstream relies on it.

issues.failure_explanation: The Koopman ground truth is E[f(X_T)|X₀=x_ℓ], whose Monte Carlo estimate averages f(y_ℓ^{(m)}). The algorithm instead averages the raw states y_ℓ^{(m)}, i.e., it estimates E[Y|X=x_ℓ]. As specified, the computed 'K_truth f' is not an approximation of Kf (for the observable f(x)=e^x used in the experiments it is a different quantity altogether), so the empirical L^∞-errors êrr_n would not measure the Koopman approximation error. This contradicts (eq:mc_testing) in the surrounding text.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the average of y_ℓ^{(m)} by the average of f(y_ℓ^{(m)}), as in (eq:mc_testing).
issues.overall_effect: The error-analysis procedure specified by alg:stochastic_kedmd_numerics does not compute the claimed ground truth as written; the numerical validation protocol is unreliable until corrected.
issues.title: Ground-truth step in the numerical algorithm averages samples instead of the observable
issues.why_classification: Single forced correction, evident from the source's own (eq:mc_testing); the algorithm's purpose and all reported conclusions are preserved.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Then, for the RKHS $\bH = H^{\nu + n/2}$ induced by the Matérn kernel $k_{\nu}$, we have the pointwise error bound
for every $\veps > 0$ and all $f \in H^{\sigma_{n,l}}$ with $\|f\|_{\bH} \leq 1$

issues.failure_explanation: In this Matérn corollary the smoothness parameter is ν (native space H^{ν+n/2}, deterministic rate h^{⌊ν⌋} per (eq:det_error_tikh_matern) and cor:det_err_matern). The stated bound instead uses the Wendland quantities l+1/2 and H^{σ_{n,l}}, with l and σ_{n,l} undefined in the corollary's context. The promised rate h^{l+1/2} is not the Matérn rate established in the appendix — the paper itself notes that, for equal smoothness, Wendland kernels gain 1/2 in the exponent over Matérn kernels — so as printed the corollary is ill-defined and, under any binding of l with l+1/2 > ⌊ν⌋, promises a faster deterministic decay than the Matérn analysis supports. The proof ('analogous to the second part of cor:reg_total_err_bound') yields the bound with h^{⌊ν⌋}, not h^{l+1/2}.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace l+1/2 by ⌊ν⌋ and H^{σ_{n,l}} by H^{ν+n/2} in (eq:reg_total_err_matern), matching (eq:det_error_tikh_matern).
issues.overall_effect: The stated regularized Matérn L^∞-error rate is wrong/ill-defined as printed; the correct statement with h^{⌊ν⌋} and H^{ν+n/2} follows from (eq:det_error_tikh_matern) combined with cor:mc_error1_tikh.
issues.title: Matérn regularized error bound stated with Wendland rate and Wendland space
issues.why_classification: Forced local correction from the source's own Matérn deterministic bound; the corollary's content is preserved with the correct rate.
